instructions:
# Stateless API Design

Design stateless, versioned HTTP APIs with contract-first tooling.

## What This Skill Does

- Authors OpenAPI 3.x specs for REST endpoints
- Validates and bundles specs with Redocly
- Enforces API style with Spectral rulesets
- Generates server stubs and typed clients

## When to Use

- Designing a new public/internal API
- Reviewing a spec for breaking changes
- Generating SDKs that match the contract

## Real Commands

```bash
# Author and validate
npx @redocly/cli init
npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml
npx swagger-cli validate openapi.yaml

# Bundle for distribution
npx @redocly/cli bundle openapi.yaml -o bundled.yaml

# Preview docs
npx @redocly/cli preview-docs openapi.yaml

# Style enforcement
npx spectral lint openapi.yaml --ruleset api-style.rules.yaml

# Generate code
openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g python-fastapi -o server/
openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g typescript-fetch -o client/
```

## Stateless API Principles

- No server-side session state; all state in request/response or client
- Version in the URL (or header) from day one
- Use idempotency keys for mutating operations
- Paginate list endpoints; document cursor semantics
- Return RFC 7807 problem details on errors

## Best Practices

- Contract-first: the spec is the source of truth
- Lint in CI with Spectral; block breaking changes
- Keep one spec per major version
- Use OpenAPI 3.1 for webhook and JSON Schema alignment
- Generate clients from the bundled spec only
